newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles arena developers may alter deal - report.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles arena developers may alter deal - report.

text.p: Developers of a proposed sports arena in Los Angeles are looking at ways of reimbursing some taxpayer costs, Los Angeles Times reported Friday.

The enhanced deal would pay some expenses the city would incur by issuing $60.5 million of bonds to acquire and clear land for the arena at the Los Angeles Convention Center, the newspaper said, citing unidentified sources.

City officials estimated that taxpayers would have to pay $4.5 million to $6 million annually over the 25-year life of the bonds if the full project, which would house the Kings hockey team and Lakers basketball team, does not materialize.
If revenues from the project cannot cover the bond payments, the city would have to step in.
"We are working really hard with city negotiators to find ways to make the deal more attractive to the city," a source on the arena side of the talks told the Times.
The source expressed confidence that the details could be resolved within the next few days.
